status_summary: Authority for SBIR and STTR lapsed after 2025-09-30 for about six months. Public Law 119-83, the Small Business Innovation and Economic Security Act, passed the Senate on 2026-03-03 and the House in mid-March and was approved on 2026-04-13; it extends the programs through 2031-09-30. The enacted text (read on GovInfo) leaves the 3.2 percent SBIR and 0.45 percent STTR set-asides unchanged, adds security-risk screening and foreign-ownership due diligence for applicants, proposal limits from FY2027 and a strategic breakthrough allocation of up to 0.50 percent of an agency's extramural R&D budget (drawn from its existing SBIR allocation) for awards of up to $30 million, and contains no requirement to spend SBIR funds on U.S.-based capital investment; CRS describes the same provisions. SBA published a notice on 2026-09-02 on updated commercialization standards, effective 2026-11-15 per the notice, with comments due 2026-10-31. Of the chapter's three asks, continuation is met by statute, while the set-aside increase and the U.S.-spending rule were not found.

timeline.event: Statutory authority for SBIR and STTR expires under the 2022 extension law; CRS later describes a lapse of about six months (exact start date not stated in the CRS product).
Trade press (BioCentury) reports Congress has reauthorized SBIR and STTR through 2031-09-30, ending a lapse of nearly six months; the article excerpt does not give chamber votes or the passage date.

Public Law 119-83 (S. 3971), the Small Business Innovation and Economic Security Act, is approved. Sec. 9 moves the SBIR and STTR authorization end date in 15 U.S.C. 638 from 2025 to 2031-09-30 and Sec. 10 extends related pilots to 2031; the text read leaves the 3.2 percent SBIR and 0.45 percent STTR set-asides unchanged, adds a Sec. 3 'strategic breakthrough allocation' of up to 0.50 percent of an agency's extramural R&D budget drawn from its SBIR allocation (agencies with SBIR spending above $100 million) for Phase II-follow-on awards of up to $30 million with a 100 percent match, adds Sec. 2 security-risk screening and foreign-ownership due diligence, and sets proposal limits from FY2027 (Sec. 4); it contains no requirement to spend funds on U.S.-based capital investment.

CRS product describes the law's strategic breakthrough awards (up to $30 million with a dollar-for-dollar match), foreign security risk screening, per-agency proposal caps from FY2027, and Phase III training for contracting staff, and lists the unchanged 3.2 and 0.45 percent set-aside rates.

SBA publishes a notice setting updated commercialization benchmarks for repeat SBIR and STTR awardees (non-SBIR revenue share of 33 percent for FY2027 and 50 percent from FY2028), effective 2026-11-15 per the notice, with comments due 2026-10-31.

title: Continue SBIR and STTR, expand set-asides, and require US-based spending
uncertainties: Stage is a judgment: the main recommendation (continue the programs) is met by statute, while the set-aside increase and the US-based spending rule are absent from the enacted text of Public Law 119-83, which pass 5 read on GovInfo through a tool summary (not line by line, and not the Statutes at Large pagination). The lapse start date is inferred from the 2025-09-30 expiration in the Mandate and the CRS description of a six-month lapse. The BioCentury article dated 2026-03-18 describes Congress as having reauthorized the programs, while the public law is dated 2026-04-13; the passage dates and vote counts were not confirmed. Whether the administration urged Congress to raise set-asides was not found. A Federal Register query for an SBA SBIR policy directive since 2025-01-20 returned no results. Whether the new commercialization benchmark has been finalized beyond the 2026-09-02 notice was not checked.
